ecus.name: Vehicle / hybrid control unit (VCU / HCU)
ecus.function: Reads driver inputs (accelerator and brake pedal, switches), arbitrates torque requests between the drive units and the battery, manages energy recovery and high-voltage state, and talks to the powertrain domain over CAN / CAN FD / Ethernet under an ASIL-C/D safety concept.

Production board count: not published in any source found.

ecus.name: Electric power steering controller (column / pinion / rack ECU)
ecus.function: Measures steering torque and angle, runs field-oriented control of a 3-phase motor (BLDC/PMSM, ~100 A at low speed and large steering angle) through a gate driver and a 6-MOSFET bridge with phase-current shunts, under a lock-step MCU and safety PMIC (ASIL-D).

pcb.layers: not published in any source found
pcb.size: Production: not published in any source found. Infineon EVALKIT_TLE9189 (evaluation kit with AURIX TC364DP, TLF35585QV and an OptiMOS 6 40 V B6 bridge) is 12.5 x 8.5 cm (evaluation board, not a production ECU).
pcb.technology: Control module (MCU board) and power module (three half-bridges of MOSFETs) linked by through-hole leads, bond wires or flex foil; a plastic carrier with lead frame can hold the large electrolytic capacitors (Electronic Design). Patents describe a separate power board on the heat sink with a signal board stacked above it, because one board carrying both needs thick copper and raises cost and thermal resistance (US 2018/0034349); EP4294138 describes stacked / split-level PCBs either side of a heat sink.
pcb.laminate: not published in any source found
pcb.boards: Typically control + power board (patents above). Tesla Model 3/Y steering racks carried two ECUs (one redundant); CNBC reported one was omitted on Shanghai-built cars during the 2022 chip shortage (Tesla did not confirm).

ecus.name: ABS / ESC brake control unit, incl. integrated brake / brake-by-wire and e-booster variants
ecus.function: Reads wheel-speed sensors, pressure and pedal sensors and the yaw / lateral-acceleration cluster, computes per-wheel brake force and drives the hydraulic unit's solenoid valves (current-controlled and on/off) and pump motor; integrated one-box and brake-by-wire variants add a 3-phase booster motor drive and regenerative-brake blending over CAN.

pcb.layers: not published in any source found
pcb.size: not published in any source found
pcb.technology: ECU PCB bolted onto the hydraulic control unit; the solenoid coil leads are soldered (or routed) to traces on the PCB, the valve sleeves press-fitted into the aluminium HCU, coils sometimes potted in a housing frame (patents). 2004 Prius skid-control ECU: a single PC board with peripherally leaded ICs in a cast housing (EDN teardown).
pcb.laminate: not published in any source found
pcb.boards: One PCB on the HCU in the patents and the Prius SCM; ESP 9 adjusts pressure through 12 solenoid valves (parts-retailer description). One-box brake-by-wire (Continental MK C1) integrates actuation, booster and ABS/ESC control in one module.

ecus.name: Airbag / restraint control unit (ACU / SDM)
ecus.function: Crash-sensing accelerometers on the board and PSI5 / DSI3 satellite sensors detect a crash; the algorithm decides within about 10 ms; an airbag system IC (power, energy reserve, satellite interfaces, safety controller) and squib drivers behind a safing switch fire the pyrotechnic loops, from an energy-reserve capacitor charged to 25-35 V if the battery is lost.

pcb.layers: not published in any source found
pcb.size: not published in any source found
pcb.technology: Energy reserve: one electrolytic capacitor sized by required energy, or two or more as airbag counts rise (patent); vented capacitor-mounting cap on the PCB (patent); example 10,000 uF Al electrolytic in an older patent. Denso SDM (2016 Prius): aluminium housing with steel plate cover. Firing supply boosted to 25-35 V (Nexperia).

notes: No production board facts (layers, size, laminate) found for VCU, EPS, ESC or ACU; placements: no public component count for any of the four boards. TechInsights / System Plus / Yole EPS, ABS and airbag reports exist behind paywalls.

No public teardown naming chips was found for Bosch iBooster / IPB / ESP hev, Continental MK C1, ZF or Tesla EPS, or any production VCU (searched in English and Chinese). Production chip identities found only for the 2004 Prius skid-control ECU (Toshiba + Mitsubishi MCUs, EDN), the Prius ACM (Denso accelerometers), a TRW ACU (EEVblog datasheet list) and the ZF-TRW 'DS84' ASIC (NHTSA EA19-001 summary).
The task's TIDA-01474 and TIDA-020018 were not found in any search result; TIDA-020106 (electro-mechanical brake, TI says applicable to EPS) and TIDUF56 (48 V drive with DRV3255-Q1) are used instead.

TLI5590 not used: the TLI prefix is Infineon's industrial grade and no EPS source names it. Wheel-speed sensors (TLE5041plusC / TLE5045iC) sit in the wheel sensor, not on the ESC board; the board carries the WSS interface (ST L9396, or in-house ASIC).
The Bosch iBooster ECU (TC / gate driver identities) and Bosch in-house valve ASIC were searched without result.
